wga:m/master/yunk_en/00cross.summary: Carved in high relief on the outside wall of Romsey Abbey, this large stone Christ stands upright on the cross with head erect and arms stretched straight out, not hanging in suffering but reigning from the tree. Above his head the Hand of God emerges from a cloud. Though weathered, the figure keeps the calm majesty of late Anglo-Saxon art, which drew on manuscript models of the Winchester school.
facts: The Web Gallery of Art dates it 1000–1020 and notes that it translates into stone models from Winchester-school manuscripts.
Christ is shown upright, head held erect and arms outstretched in welcome, with the Hand of God emerging from the clouds above him.
It may originally have stood inside the earlier Saxon church and been reset on the Norman building, where a modern canopy now shelters it.
wga:m/master/yunk_en/00cross.notes: Dating varies (first half of the 11th century; Talbot Rice 1000–20; some link it to the church of 967).
